subject: AcmePay: Deterministic latency SLA + audit trace retention - prioritization request
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-09-14T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: AcmePay: Deterministic latency SLA + audit trace retention - prioritization request

Team —

Quick context: AcmePay (Jamal + Priya) moved to pricing approval but have two blocking technical asks in the SOW that are gating signature:
- Deterministic 99th percentile latency for their auth and fraud-check routes (target: <= 80ms p99)
- Retention of inference traces & request metadata for 90 days for their auditors (SOC2 appendix) with export capability to their S3/KMS

Deal size: ~$1.2M ARR; legal/procurement timeline: want signed by end of September. I attached the SOW + the SLA spec they sent.

What I need from Product + Eng:
- A defensible Minimum Viable Feature (MVF) we can commit to for a canary (what exactly do we ship to start?)
- Realistic timeline (weeks) and minimal headcount estimate (dev + QA + SRE) to deliver the MVF for a limited pilot
- Major technical blockers / open security/compliance questions (esp. around 90-day trace retention + KMS integration)
- Clear acceptance criteria we can show Acme for sign-off and for legal to accept in the SOW

Commercial ask: if we can commit to a pilot plan and a target date I can keep the close on track; if not, they will likely push to a competitor who offered a partial SLA.

Requested by: EOD 9/16 so I can update Jamal in our Thursday call.

Attachments: Acme_SOW_draft.pdf, Latency_SLA_Spec.xlsx

Thanks —
Vanessa
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmePay: Deterministic latency SLA + audit trace retention - prioritization request

Thanks for the context, Vanessa —

A few clarifying questions before Karthik and I estimate effort:
1) Which API routes are in-scope for the p99 SLA? Auth (token issue), fraud-check, or both? Are we talking per-request SLA for initial response or end-to-end (including downstream calls)?
2) Do they require hard enforcement (we must never exceed 80ms p99) or an operational target (we aim for <=80ms and provide fallbacks)?
3) For traces: what fields are required by auditors (raw inputs, model outputs, model version, prompt metadata, session IDs)? Do they allow redaction of PII before retention?

Initial thought for MVF (opinionated):
- Route affinity + pre-warmed warm pools for the two in-scope routes (reduces cold-start variance)
- Prefix/KV caching for deterministic path (where applicable) + request-tagging for trace exports
- Export pipeline to S3 (customer-managed bucket) with retention enforced on their side OR optional retention on Redwood for 90 days if they require us to hold it

If they need a contractual hard SLA at 80ms p99 across shared capacity, that implies dedicated capacity or extremely conservative resource reservations. Karthik — can you outline the engineering delta between the MVF above vs. a hard contractual guarantee?

—Marissa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-15T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmePay: AcmePay SLA/prioritization - engineering impact and rough estimate

Thanks — quick engineering read:

Scope assumptions (based on Marissa's MVF): auth + fraud routes only; p99 target is operational, not a legal penalty clause. Retention is export-only to customer S3 preferred.

Workstreams and considerations:
1) Dedicated route affinity + pre-warmed workers: requires routing policy + warm-pool orchestration. Complexity: medium. Effort: ~3-4 dev-weeks (runtime + autoscaler + config surface).
2) Prefix/KV cache path & keying for auth flow: low-medium (some models already support prefix cache) — ~2 dev-weeks + QA.
3) Trace tagging + export pipeline to S3 (with optional server-side encryption with customer's KMS): medium — ~3 dev-weeks; requires security review for KMS integration.
4) SLO testing harness + canary automation + telemetry dashboards: ~2 dev-weeks + 1 SRE engineer half-time for canary run.

Total rough engineering time: 10-12 dev-weeks (can overlap; with 2 engineers dedicated could be 6-8 calendar weeks). This is MVF (no hard legal SLA).

If they require a contractually-backed hard p99 =<80ms on shared hosted fleet, that effectively implies: dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs), conservative headroom, and formal runbook + penalty clauses. Incremental delta: +4-8 dev-weeks to build isolation/hard reservations and additional testing, plus ongoing cost.

Risks / blockers:
- Memory/resource pressure from per-tenant warm pools can increase cost significantly for us or the customer.
- KMS integration for customer-managed keys needs security sign-off (PKI/KMS cert exchange work).
- Acceptance tests from Acme must be deterministic (we'll need a test harness they agree to run).

Estimate to show to Acme for a canary that demonstrates p99 improvements (non-contractual): 4 weeks to deliver a limited pilot if we accept scope reductions (route-limited, pilot on dedicated pilot capacity).

I'll add a short tech note if helpful.

—Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamal Reynolds <jamal@acmepay.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmepay.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmePay: Deterministic latency SLA + audit trace retention - prioritization request

Appreciate the quick read and the options. To push the commercial forward I'd like to propose a compromise we can offer Acme this week:

Proposal (canary-first, limited commit):
- Redwood will deliver MVF limited to auth + fraud routes, running on a small dedicated pilot pool (separate tenant reservation)
- Enable prefix cache + pre-warmed workers for the pilot; instrumented telemetry and a shared dashboard
- Export trace data to Acme-managed S3 (customers are responsible for retention) — if Acme requires Redwood to hold data for 90 days we will reassess costs and legal terms separately
- Pilot window: 2 weeks of production traffic at 10% of their auth volume (or equivalent traffic profile). Acceptance criteria: p99 improvement to <=100ms (we can set 100ms for pilot; Acme can choose to escalate to contractual 80ms if pilot metrics are reproducible)

Commercial asks from Acme: they want a date to show procurement; can you commit to an internal target to deliver pilot config and a runbook by 2027-09-21? If we have something demonstrable by then I can keep their signature from slipping past EoM.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2027-091

If we can do a 4-week rapid pilot (Karthik's 4-week smaller-scope path), I'll get Jamal to sign a pilot acceptance and cover any incremental infra cost for the dedicated pilot. Monica — can you prepare a draft acceptance test plan for the pilot?

Thanks — pressing on timeline here.
Vanessa
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamal Reynolds <jamal@acmepay.com>
Date: 2027-09-16T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmePay pilot acceptance criteria and next steps

Will do — I'll draft a pilot acceptance plan and checklist by EOD 9/17 and align with Jamal on the specific traffic profile. Key items I'll include:
- Exact endpoints and payloads in-scope
- Baseline telemetry to capture (latency histograms, model version, request tags)
- Data elements required in trace export and permitted redactions
- Canary runbook (rollout %, rollback criteria, escalation contacts)
- Success criteria for pilot (we'll use the 100ms p99 pilot target Vanessa proposed unless Engineering flags it as unrealistic)

Also will coordinate procurement language for infra-cost coverage (they agreed to pilot infra cost during sales).

Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
